cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and the pattern is being worked closer and further down.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Tonight or this week, give an hour to the pattern you love with nothing you need from it. No output, no end. Put it down when it's done.
cells.core:
You can go further into a pattern than people can follow. You take it down past the part that translates, past the point where you could explain it to anybody, and you stay there — not to prove anything, and it isn't an escape. Seeing how it actually works is the pleasure, and you recognize what you find when you find it.

The cost is that no one can follow you in. When you come back up with something real, there was no company down there. The suggestion here is an hour with the pattern for no reason — not to solve it, not to bring back a report. What you find can be yours first, before it has to be anything to anybody.
cells.sheetLine: You can go deeper than anyone can follow, and that's the gift.
cells.verb: going all the way down into the pattern past where language reaches
cells.place: somewhere the pattern is right and the comparison is gone

cells.tense: You are bracing to be understood at some future point when they have finally caught up.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Bring one piece you've figured out back to where it can be said plainly — one plan, one rule, one frame — and state that once. Then wait, and stop building.
cells.core:
You're taking the pattern further than was asked for, and then waiting to be understood. The working goes deeper than it needs to, and the explaining waits for later, when they have finally caught up. So the case gets built in your head instead of said, or it gets said before it was asked for and lands as a lecture. What comes across isn't what you made; it's pressure to agree.

The depths don't have to be handed over. Say the piece that matters, in plain words, once, and stop. If it doesn't land, that's something to work with — not proof the whole thing failed. The pattern can sit outside your head, waiting for whatever comes back, without getting more elaborate.
cells.sheetLine: You keep going deeper, then wait for them to catch up.
cells.verb: going all the way down into the pattern past where language reaches
cells.place: somewhere the pattern is right and the comparison is gone

cells.tense: You were still standing at a door that had already closed behind you.
cells.act: share the joy with the people it belongs to
cells.ask: Tell someone about one good thing that happened, even flatly. Just a sentence about the good thing, not a talk about what it means.
cells.core:
The pattern goes all the way down, and nothing reaches out for it. You see how a thing works and it stays inside, and taking one of those out somewhere — a meeting, a home, a table — came back as a strange thing to say, so you got quieter about how you know things. That habit stands down around people, and the depth has somewhere to go, which is back in.

Telling people keeps a version of you among them without making a production of it. One good thing, said out loud, no lesson on top. You're not trying to become somebody else. You're putting one foot back among the people the pattern belongs to.
cells.sheetLine: You went quiet, and the pattern went quiet with you.

cells.tense: You are down in something that holds you, and from the outside you would call it being alone.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Take ten minutes tonight and sit with what you know about this — no noodling, no notes, no next step. When it's done, it's done.
cells.core:
You go so far into a pattern that it stops being a subject and starts being a place. Down there, comparisons drop away and the thing is simply the way it is, and you don't experience this as a mood — you'd say you were reading, or thinking, or just getting on with work. Your account of those hours is a lot more modest than what's actually happening in them.

The quiet at the bottom is not a symptom. It's the feeling of being where the pattern is right and everything else is left at the surface. Sitting with what you know there — not to turn it into anything, just sit with it — is the way back. What you find down there first came from that quiet, and it's still yours.

attempts.check: The claim in my draft the record doesn't support: that the person has lost or gains a felt sense of belonging. The record says the gift is going deeper into pattern than anyone else will follow, and it doesn't say how that feels or what it has cost. A reader could reasonably say the deep trance is deliberate — the only way to get anything done — and my Too Much draft should not overrule that account. The asks survive being wrong: each is one small visible act, useful whether or not the reading is right. The sentence I had to cut was one that praised the person for the method I invented for them — it served me, not them.
